title: Game Record (teardown)
description:
One researched game in a research corpus: <corpus>/games/<game-id>.json. The discovery module's input format for game-level research, the way snapshots are for portal facts. A record is a set of dated sessions (a timed play, a listing read, a store page) and the facet codings each session supports, every coding in the shared research vocabulary (core/reference/research-vocabulary.yaml).

A coding is `observed` when its excerpt is the thing itself - a portal's own category tag, a stopwatch reading, an ad the observer saw offered - and `interpreted` when it is the observer's reading of a capture (a theme seen on a thumbnail, a tone, a fantasy). Interpreted codings become derived claims whose parent is the session's own observed claim, so an interpretation never passes as an observation. An observation without an excerpt is refused.

A record marked `fixture: true` is test data. It is never real evidence: every claim it yields is tagged `fixture` and the report says so.

listing_names.description: Names the game is listed under on portals, in any locale, so listing observations join this record.

observer.description: Role or person who observed. An agent may observe; it may not invent.

viewport.description: e.g. '390x844 phone, throttled 4G'. Required in practice for played sessions.

capture_uri.description: Recording, screenshot set or notes the session's excerpts can be checked against.

note.description: What was done, verbatim enough to re-check: the session's own excerpt.

value.description: A vocabulary id (facet kind `one`), a list of ids (`many`), or a number in the facet's unit (`number`).

notes.description: Free observations worth keeping that no facet counts: a standout strength, an exception to a pattern, something that felt bad. Kept as observed claims, never counted.
